solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Don't declare uranium advances in rogue state capital

parts.note: in cricket, a side that does not declare its innings will bat on

indicators.note: one letter moving forward within a word rearranges that word's order, here only a single letter shifting position

parts.note: taken as written; its U (uranium) is then moved one place earlier

explanation.surface: A rogue state is being told not to announce that its uranium enrichment is progressing.
explanation.walkthrough: To declare in cricket is to end your innings voluntarily, so not declaring means you BAT ON. U is the symbol for uranium; moving it ahead of the G turns ROGUE into ROUGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Baton Rouge is the capital city of Louisiana in the United States.

clue.text: Pager — sound of alarm's piercing; one's used to working with buzzers

definitions.text: one's used to working with buzzers

indicators.note: something piercing a thing goes right into it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a pager is a beeper
EEK is a cry of alarm

explanation.surface: A pager sounding an alarm interrupts someone used to working with electronic buzzers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pager' and 'buzzers' both suggest electronic gadgets; the buzzers are actually bees, which is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees buzz, so a person who tends hives works daily with buzzing insects; a playful cryptic description.

clue.text: Organ piece for Charlie, jazz fan, No 1 in America

parts.note: 'bound for' and 'bound to' mean the same, so for can stand for TO
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

indicators.note: number one in a word is its first letter, the one standing at the head

parts.note: the opening letter of America

explanation.surface: A piece of organ music is chosen for Charlie, a jazz lover who is top in America.
explanation.walkthrough: TO + C + CAT + A. 'Cat' for a jazz fan is jive-era slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuosic keyboard composition, Bach's famous one being written for the organ.

clue.text: Downgrade envoy after the Holy See becomes discontented?

indicators.note: coming after means placed behind, which fixes the order of the two pieces
to lose one's contents is to be emptied, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the Holy See is the papacy in Rome, so ROME, emptied out
a legate is a papal envoy

explanation.surface: The Vatican is unhappy and demotes its ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: The Holy See is identified with Rome, the seat of the papacy, which is emptied to its outer letters. 'Discontented' looks like a mood word but means emptied of contents.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate someone is to move them to a lower rank or position, which is to demote them.

clue.text: Ramshackle Armenian yurt? Pal, that won't do for our House!

definitions.text: that won't do for our House
definitions.note: adjectival phrase: language not allowed in Parliament

indicators.note: something ramshackle is tumbledown and disordered, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend is told a shabby Armenian tent would never be fit to house British lawmakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our House' is the House of Commons; the surface makes it sound like a building where a yurt won't do.
explanation.definitionFit: Unparliamentary language is speech, like calling a member a liar, that the Speaker rules out of order in the Commons.

clue.text: Young winger last to tie end of bootlace

indicators.note: last means final, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of tie
an aglet is the plastic or metal tip on the end of a lace

explanation.surface: Someone is told to finish lacing a boot by tying off the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of bootlace' looks like a single-letter selection, but it is the whole word AGLET; the selected letter comes from 'tie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle is a bird, a creature with wings, so a young winger in crossword terms.

clue.text: Hard cheese — poor lad lost $1

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, broken up, so the letters to remove are scattered rather than together
what is lost is no longer there, so those letters drop out wherever they stand

parts.note: hard cheese is British slang for bad luck
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A lad commiserates with a poor boy who has lost a dollar: hard cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese' is a British way of saying 'tough luck'. 'Poor' tells you the letters of LAD are scattered through BAD LUCK rather than together.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck is informal American slang for a dollar, one unit of US currency.

clue.text: Bits of skeleton a tailless dog buried in good faith

indicators.note: something buried in a thing lies inside it, enclosed on all sides

parts.note: a skeleton is made of bones
taken as written

indicators.note: without its tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Fido is the stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A dog buries some bones, with its owner trusting all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: FIDO loses its last letter to give FID; A + FID goes inside BONES. Fido is the conventional dog's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fides is Latin for genuine honesty of intention, the sense of acting sincerely and honestly.

clue.text: Business fury involving one thousand fee added to drinks bill

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: rage is fury
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A company is furious about a thousand-pound charge on its bar tab.
explanation.walkthrough: K for a thousand comes from kilo; 'business' gives the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Corkage is the charge a restaurant makes for opening and serving wine that a customer brought in.

clue.text: Sit back to eat cold, whole shellfish

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows the others
going back means running the other way, so the letters read from right to left

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose
C for cold, as on a tap
the whole is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone leans back to eat a whole cold shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sit back' reads as relaxing, but 'back' turns the word for sitting round before it swallows the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Escallop is an older spelling of scallop, a bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped shell.

clue.text: Aristocrats replacing key framework

indicators.note: replacing means one thing takes another's place, swapping a single letter

parts.note: the gentry are the upper classes
A is a musical key; it takes the place of E, another key

explanation.surface: Members of the nobility are swapping out a central structural element.
explanation.walkthrough: In GENTRY the key E is swapped for the key A. Musical keys run A to G, so any of those letters can be a key.
explanation.definitionFit: A gantry is a bridge-like overhead structure supporting cranes, signals or rocket equipment.

clue.text: Isaac's son second to visit Arab lands to the west

indicators.note: west is leftward on a map, so in an across clue the letters travel right to left
a visitor goes inside a place, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: the United Arab Emirates
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A biblical son briefly travels west to Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside UAE to make UASE, which then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Isaac's elder twin son was the hairy hunter who sold his birthright to Jacob.

clue.text: Guy initially mad keen to keep Florida condo with outside space

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the first letter of Guy

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: mad keen means very enthusiastic
Fla. is the traditional abbreviation for Florida

explanation.surface: A man is very keen to have a Florida condominium with a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: Florida here is the older abbreviation FLA, not the two-letter postal FL. 'Mad keen' is British for extremely enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flat is a ground-floor apartment with its own garden, so a condo with outdoor space.

clue.text: Exercise, regularly painful hard work requisite for cook?

parts.note: PE is physical education

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, skipping the rest

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of painful
toil is hard work

explanation.surface: A cook needs exercise and painful hard graft, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: PE + ANU + TOIL. The question mark marks the definition as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundnut-derived oil is a staple frying medium, one of the things a cook needs in the kitchen.

clue.text: Horrible experience in which mounted champion gets beheaded?

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a champion is a knight, a mounted warrior
what a mounted fighter rides on is a horse, here a mare

explanation.surface: A dreadful ordeal in which a champion on horseback is decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT loses its K and sits on top of a MARE, as a mounted knight would in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any terrifying or very unpleasant ordeal.

clue.text: Yet more weird food — starter binned

indicators.note: throwing away the starter means the first letter goes

parts.note: fodder is food, especially for livestock

explanation.surface: Even stranger food is served, and the first course is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: FODDER loses its F. 'Starter' sounds like the first course of a meal but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, meaning stranger or more peculiar than before.

clue.text: Well-bred individual coming from Timor, Aceh or Serang?

indicators.note: something coming from the words emerges out of them, straddling them as one continuous run

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Timor, all of Aceh and or, and the start of Serang

explanation.surface: A person of good breeding comes from one of three Indonesian places.
explanation.walkthrough: Timor, Aceh and Serang are all places in Indonesia, chosen to make the surface look like a geography question.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughbred racing animals are bred for pedigree, so one is literally a well-bred creature.

clue.text: DJ's companion gave somebody a shiner, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound counts, not spelling

parts.note: a shiner is a black eye, so giving one is to have blacked an eye

explanation.surface: A disc jockey's friend punched someone in the eye, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ here is a dinner jacket, not a disc jockey; a black tie is worn with one. A shiner is a bruised eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket is worn with a black bow tie, so the two go together as formal evening dress.

clue.text: Storm passing over northern mountains

indicators.note: passing over something covers it from either side, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to storm is to rage
N for northern

explanation.surface: A storm moves across mountains in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside RAGE. 'Storm' reads as a noun but works as the verb rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a connected chain or line of peaks, as in a mountain range.

clue.text: Perhaps blue permit featured in articles

indicators.note: featured in something means appearing within it, so one piece sits inside others

parts.note: A and THE are the two English articles
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: Perhaps a blue permit appears in some documents.
explanation.walkthrough: LET inside A THE. A Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Blue at Oxford or Cambridge is awarded for sporting representation, so one example of a sportsperson.

clue.text: Old-fashioned adhesive manufactured from camel spit

indicators.note: manufacturing makes a new product from raw material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old glue was made out of camel saliva.
explanation.walkthrough: The disgusting surface invites you to picture glue made from camel saliva; it is simply the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Emplastic is an archaic adjective meaning sticky or adhesive, used of plasters and glues.

clue.text: First Lady: "I'm obliged to ingest nerve gas"

indicators.note: ingesting takes something into the body, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you, which is what 'I'm obliged' means
sarin is a nerve agent

explanation.surface: A president's wife claims she must swallow poison gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is everyday British for 'thanks', so 'I'm obliged' gives it. 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife but means the leading woman of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The empress of Russia was the wife of the tsar, the leading woman of the realm.

clue.text: Right-leaning type?

parts.note: surface reading: a person with conservative political views
setter's reading: a typeface whose letters slope to the right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a kind of person, and 'right-leaning' like politics; in printing, type is lettering, and sloped lettering leans right.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping printed letters, used for emphasis, are angled toward the right of the page.

clue.text: Craft movie hit I can't rent around

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece holds another
rent means torn apart, so the letters are ripped up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
E.T. is Spielberg's film about an alien

explanation.surface: A film-maker cannot afford to rent a hit movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like hiring, but means torn; the jumbled letters wrap around ET. The surface also hints at the hit film Titanic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the ocean liner that sank in 1912, and a ship is a craft.

clue.text: Shampoo and cut for receding husband

indicators.note: something receding moves backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: sawed, or saw, is cut
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A hairdresser offers a shampoo and cut for a man whose hairline is receding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receding' looks like a hairline but turns SAW round; H for husband is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To shampoo hair is to clean it with soap and water, so the verb and noun match.

clue.text: Express sorrow about European wife's security

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: bail is money given as security for an accused person
W is the standard abbreviation for wife
E for European
surface padding: the possessive just links the pieces

explanation.surface: Someone laments the financial security of a European woman's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIL goes around E and W, although it appears last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewail is to lament, mourning loudly or showing great regret over something.

clue.text: With leader absent, badinage beginning to inspire soldiers at the front

indicators.note: losing the leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: badinage is playful banter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of inspire
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Without their commander, jokey chat lifts the spirits of troops on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: BANTER drops its B, then I and OR follow. OR, other ranks, is the standard crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior is an anatomical and formal term for positioned toward the front.

clue.text: Reported grain yield

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the sound of a word is wanted

parts.note: a grain of corn is a seed

explanation.surface: A farmer announces the harvest return from his corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grain yield' reads as a crop total; 'yield' is the verb meaning give up, and 'grain' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a point is to give it up, surrendering it to another party.

clue.text: Barrow boys backed English horse

parts.note: Clyde Barrow was the outlaw partner of Bonnie Parker

indicators.note: moving back means going in reverse, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: lads are boys
E for English

explanation.surface: Street-market traders bet on an English racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow boys are British street traders selling from carts, but here Barrow is Clyde Barrow of Bonnie and Clyde. 'Backed' sounds like betting but reverses LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clydesdale is a heavy draught breed of horse from Scotland; 'English' belongs to the wordplay.
